# Colony History
[italic]A short history of Shepherds' Pride for new arrivals, as the Herald's archive tells it.[/italic]
## The Survey LV-112 went into the catalogue as a wet, green world on the far edge of the Neroid Sector: thick jungle, one long river basin and native life in every pool of it. There was nothing under the soil worth the trip. What the survey teams brought back was the life itself, and the United Americas chose to keep it rather than clear it.
## The Reserve The world was chartered as a wildlife reserve, and the [bold]Colonial Wilderness Preservation Service[/bold] was sent to hold it. The CWPS rangers are still the law here. They keep the perimeter, patrol the preserve and write the tickets: no poaching, no dumping, no overfishing. The terms are posted at the [netlink="Colony Administration" link="admin.colony.gov/charter"].
## The River Towns - The first ranger posts grew into [bold]North Colony[/bold] and [bold]South Colony[/bold], strung along the river road. - The licensed [bold]fishery[/bold] gave families a living, and the chapel, the hospital and the South Colony theatre followed. - The [bold]Riverboat Casino[/bold] brought money from off-world, and with it people the rangers cannot easily fine.
## The Carp Somebody, years back, emptied an off-world carp tank into the river. They bred faster than anything native, ate the native fry out of the shallows and grew big enough to take a hand off a careless angler. The CWPS has paid a bounty on every tail ever since, and the bar by the water took its name from them. The carp are still winning.
## The Company Lease Weyland-Yutani holds a research lease inside the reserve. Its lab sits behind its own fence with its own guards, close to the experimental sensor tower. Every question the Herald has put to the Company about what is studied there has come back with the same answer: botany.
## The Press The Herald keeps the archive of Shepherds' Pride from the journalist's office in town, and keeps it open to anyone who asks. Somebody has to write down what the reserve is for, and who is getting paid from it.
